learning_outcomes.text: Understand the representation of information in computers.
Know how the different subsystems of a computer (processor, memory and input/output) work.
Write simple programs in assembly language.
Know at a basic level how computers interconnect to form computer networks.
Knowledge of the structure, organization, functioning of computer systems and their application for solving engineering problems.
Knowledge of the interconnection of computer systems and their application for solving engineering problems.
Ability to solve problems within their area of study.
Capacity for abstraction: ability to create and use models that reflect real situations.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment of the theoretical part (NTeo)
Continuous assessment of the practical part (NPrac)

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final grade (NotaConvOrdinaria) is 0.5 * NTeo + 0.4 * NPrac + 0.1 * NPro, provided NTeo is >= 4.0; otherwise, it is the minimum of 4.5 and the formula result. A minimum active attendance of 80% to laboratory practices and group tutorials is required for NPrac. For extraordinary calls, an explicit theory exam (NExTeo) and practical exam (NExPrac) are required, with NExTeo needing to be >= 5.0 to pass, and NPrac can be retained if it was > 5.0 from the course. For differentiated evaluation, a final theory exam (NDifTeo) and practical exam (NDifPrac) are mandatory, with NDifTeo needing to be >= 5.0 to take the practical exam; the final grade is 0.5 * NDifTeo + 0.5 * NDifPrac. Fraudulent activity in any assessment will result in a 0 for that call.
